headline: ChatGPT-6 Astra plays World of Warcraft 'blind' and clears Orc starting zone in 40 mins with 0 deaths
summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra completed the Orc starting zone on a private WoW server in 40 minutes without seeing a single rendered frame, relying solely on network traffic and quest data.
details: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra AI model successfully cleared the Orc starting area in World of Warcraft (WoW) in just 40 minutes, achieving 0 deaths. The model accomplished this feat using the open-source agent-wow client on a private server.

Crucially, the AI played the entire zone without seeing a single rendered frame. It relied entirely on network traffic and quest data pulled directly from the server's own files, using a single prompt in Codex with agent-wow.

Agent-wow is an open-source AzerothCore WoW client designed for autonomous AI agent players. It does not define gameplay mechanics but provides a module system for agents to build their own movement, combat, and interaction logic.

The developer ran OpenAI's flagship model with extra high reasoning effort, just below the maximum setting. WoW was chosen for its blend of long-term strategy and short-term tactics, with future goals including AI agents clearing Icecrown Citadel.

The agent built a single module to capture 28 types of server messages, which it kept in memory. A Python script then polled these messages to construct the agent's understanding of the world and send back actions.

For quest data, the agent directly mined information like quest givers, turn-ins, and spawn points from AzerothCore's SQL files. This method is arguably more direct than a human researching on fan sites like Wowhead, as it uses the server's live data.

The agent demonstrated strategic planning, working through prerequisite quest chains, selling junk, equipping upgrades, and training abilities. It also picked up and completed multiple quests simultaneously in the zone's final cave.

Pathfinding was handled by a C++ helper that used AzerothCore's navigation mesh files and the Detour pathfinding library. The developer noted the agent's pathfinding abilities were "optimal," even allowing it to exploit map bugs.

This isn't the first game the model has tackled; it previously played Portal using screenshots. However, this WoW run was unique in its 'blind' approach, relying purely on data rather than visual input.

headline_marked: [[Zinc whiskers]] cause silent contamination under AI data center floors
headline: Zinc whiskers cause silent contamination under AI data center floors
summary: Microscopic zinc filaments growing from underfloor hardware are causing intermittent short circuits and disrupting multi-week AI model training runs in large-scale data centers.
details: Technicians inspecting a 2-megawatt AI cluster found a metallic sheen under the raised floor. Within 90 minutes of restoring full load, nodes began registering intermittent short-circuit events, disrupting multi-week AI model training runs. These failures included non-reproducible ECC errors, GPU resets, and abrupt job terminations on liquid-cooled servers with NVIDIA H100 GPUs.

Particle analysis revealed microscopic zinc filaments, 0.5 to 2 millimeters long, originating from the zinc-plated steel pedestals and stringers. These conductive whiskers were dislodged by high-velocity airflow from dense rack exhaust, reaching speeds exceeding 400 feet per minute. The particles then entered server intakes, causing critical hardware issues.

The contamination was aggressive due to elevated static pressure (0.08 to 0.12 inches of water column) under the floor, accelerating particles into server intakes. Once inside, whiskers bridged fine-pitch traces on GPU daughter cards and voltage regulator modules, triggering protection circuits. Failures clustered during peak training epochs, directly linking computational load, airflow, and whisker mobilization.

Recovery involved systematic replacement of affected boards, installation of conductive-particle filters, and switching to non-whisker-forming coatings like powder-coated steel. This incident shows how routine maintenance can redistribute conductive debris, especially with the extreme airflow demands of modern AI infrastructure. Airborne-particle counters detected elevated metallic particulate counts for weeks post-event.

Legacy raised-floor systems use galvanized steel, where a 5-15 micrometer zinc coating protects against corrosion but introduces residual compressive stresses. These stresses drive the spontaneous formation of zinc whiskers, thin filamentary crystals that extrude perpendicular to the surface. Growth starts at microscopic defects and can take several years to reach problematic lengths.
